title: Exact native adic pullback and Frobenius mate compatibility
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Use the coefficient sheaves $B_X,B_Y$, their module-sheaf categories $\mathcal A_X,\mathcal A_Y$ and geometric Frobenii $F_X,F_Y$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $L=\bar f^*:\mathcal A_Y\to\mathcal A_X$ be the actual module inverse image $B_X\otimes_{\bar f^{-1}B_Y}\bar f^{-1}(-)$, and let $R=\bar f_*:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_Y$ use the coefficient map $B_Y\to\bar f_*B_X$ given by precomposition of locally finite continuous functions. Equip them with the canonical ringed-topos adjunction $L\dashv R$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$.

The functor $L$ is additive and exact, and $R$ is additive. The native Frobenius functors $P_T=(F_T^{-1})_*\cong F_T^*$ on $\mathcal A_T$ for $T=X,Y$ are additive autoequivalences. Let
$$e:P_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}LP_Y,\qquad b:P_YR\xrightarrow{\sim}RP_X$$
be the canonical module comparisons used to lift these functors to Weil sheaves in the framework: $b$ is the direct-image composition comparison for $\bar f F_X^{-1}=F_Y^{-1}\bar f$, and $e$ is the pullback composition comparison for $F_Y\bar f=\bar f F_X$, conjugated by the specified identifications $P_T\cong F_T^*$. Products of functors in this statement denote ordinary composition, with the rightmost functor applied first. The actual comparison $b$ is the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $e^{-1}$: for every $M\in\mathcal A_X$,
$$b_M=R(P_X(\varepsilon_M))\circ R(e^{-1}_{RM})\circ\eta_{P_YRM}:P_YRM\longrightarrow RP_XM.$$
The comparisons are those of `ProEtale.adicUpperStarGeometricFiberMapCompFrobeniusIso` and `ProEtale.adicLowerStarGeometricFiberMapCompFrobeniusIso`, with the coefficient actions specified above.

proof.text: Put $J=\bar f$, $a=F_X$, $b=F_Y$. Their relation $Ja=bJ$ follows by projecting $\bar f=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_k$ and $F_T=\mathrm{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Frob}_k^{-1}$ to the two factors; the first projections are $f_0$ and the second are $\operatorname{Frob}_k^{-1}$. Composing with the inverses gives $Ja^{-1}=b^{-1}J$. Apply [lem-sf-native-adic-pullback-exact-lisse] to the scheme morphism $g=J:\bar X\to\bar Y$; its coefficient sheaves are the $B_X,B_Y$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] and its coefficient map is the same map $\alpha_J:J^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ adjoint to precomposition $B_Y\to J_*B_X$ (the framework names this adjoint, with $J^{-1}$ the geometric inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]). That lemma gives that $\alpha_J$ is an isomorphism and that $L(M)=B_X\otimes_{J^{-1}B_Y}J^{-1}M$ is exact. $L$ is additive: $J^{-1}$ is additive on abelian sheaves and $B_X\otimes_{J^{-1}B_Y}(-)$ is additive, both by construction on Hom groups. The ringed-topos adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] for the morphism of topoi $J$ with ring map $c=\alpha_J$ has as left adjoint exactly this tensor formula and as right adjoint $J_*$ with the action through the adjunct of $\alpha_J$, which is the precomposition map; so it is the specified $L\dashv R$, not an adjunction with independently chosen unit or counit.

source.place: Module.lean lines 117–178; UpperStar.lean lines 263–312 (upperStarAdicConstantSheafIso). Geometric commutation uses the two product projections.

proof.text: Direct image sends a module map to its precomposition on sections, so $R(u+v)=R(u)+R(v)$ and $R(0)=0$. For $T=X,Y$, put $P_T=(F_T^{-1})_*$ and $A_T=(F_T)_*$. The composition comparisons identify $A_TP_T$ and $P_TA_T$ with the identity. They are module maps: on each section precomposition sends $sm$ to $(s\circ t)(m\circ t)$, exactly the prescribed coefficient action. Their inverse identities and triangle equations reduce to the unique maps between iterated fibre products with the same projections. Thus they give the specified additive inverse equivalences, with unit the inverse of $A_TP_T\cong\mathrm{id}$. Both $F_T^*$ and $P_T$ are left adjoint to $A_T$; the comparison $F_T^*\cong P_T$ is the unique one whose conjugate is $\mathrm{id}_{A_T}$ under the conjugation bijection. This is precisely adicUpperStarIsoLowerStarInv, by its definition using leftAdjointUniq.

Use $A=a_*$, $B=b_*$, $P=(a^{-1})_*$ and $Q=(b^{-1})_*$. Denote by $C:RA\to BR$ the direct-image composition comparison through $(Ja)_*=(bJ)_*$. Expand the specified $e^{-1}:LQ\to PL$ into its five defining factors, in application order: replace $Q$ by $b^*$; use $Lb^*\cong(bJ)^*$; change along $bJ=Ja$; use $(Ja)^*\cong a^*L$; replace $a^*$ by $P$. The two replacement comparisons were normalized in Step 2 to conjugate to identities. For each composition factor, the adicUpperStarComp definition is inverse conjugation of adicLowerStarComp; for the equality factor, adicUpperStarCongr is equality transport and its conjugate is the inverse equality transport of direct images. These are definitions of the actual named maps in Module.lean, not assertions that arbitrary comparison maps are normalized.

proof.text: Conjugation reverses composition. Apply mate pasting to the five factors in Step 3, including the whiskered identity conjugates at the ends. Under the composite adjunctions $PL\dashv RA$ and $LQ\dashv BR$ the result is the three-factor direct-image word $RA\to(Ja)_*=(bJ)_*\to BR$, namely $C$. No tensor coefficient is changed: every constituent uses the same precomposition map. This computes the full conjugate of the specified $e^{-1}$, and not merely the existence of an isomorphism of its source and target.

The actual $b:QR	o RP$ is the direct-image word through $(b^{-1}J)_*=(Ja^{-1})_*$. Forget its module actions. The unit-square lemma, applied to $J,a,b$ and the underlying abelian sheaf of $M$, gives $C_{PM}\circ R(
u^a_M)=B(b_M)\circ
u^b_{RM}$. The underlying units are exactly $
u^a,
u^b$: adicLowerStarEquivalence defines them by the same composition and identity maps. The equality therefore holds as a module equality, since forgetting a module map is injective. Under $Q\dashv B$, the transpose of $b_M$ is $B(b_M)\circ
u^b_{RM}$, so the displayed equation says that $b$ is the inverse mate of $C$ for $P\dashv A$, $Q\dashv B$. Equivalently, the mate of $b$ along these equivalences equals $C$. This deduction uses the unit characterization of the mate bijection, without assuming that the direct-image exchange is already the desired mate under $L\dashv R$.

Apply the iterated-square-mate identity to $\alpha=e^{-1}:LQ\to PL$, with the horizontal adjunctions both $L\dashv R$ and the vertical adjunctions $Q\dashv B$ and $P\dashv A$. Its first mate is $\beta:QR\to RP$; its second mate is, by that identity, the conjugate under $PL\dashv RA$ and $LQ\dashv BR$ computed in Step 4, hence $C$. Step 5 says the second mate of the actual $b$ is also $C$. Injectivity of this mate bijection gives $\beta=b$. Expanding the first mate definition at $M$ now gives exactly
$$b_M=R(P(\varepsilon_M))\circ R(e^{-1}_{RM})\circ\eta_{QRM}.$$
Here $P=P_X$, $Q=P_Y$, and the units and counits are the specified ones from Step 1. Together with Steps 1–2 this proves every clause.
